observations.statement: The bounded-weight odd minimum uses native and arithmetic inequalities before stage selection: coarse divisibility controls large weight, an attained integer minimum controls finitely bounded weights on an ultrafilter set, and a single stage is chosen only after the finite precision and weight budgets. No one stage controls all weights.

The nonempty seed argument fixes the fresh even twist and quadratic field before address dimension. The forward even-unit result gives corank zero and the class sum gives corank one over the quadratic field. Waldspurger transfers coefficient valuations between the two signed sources. Under the no-seed assumption the trace construction divides by the integer two twice, with the determinant difference only asserted even.

The trace contradiction checks every theta convolution term, uses a fresh prime with matching actual joint Galois and label data, and computes the unary-subtracted coefficient. The resulting mod-eight congruence contradicts the explicit halving obstruction and exact four-element two-primary reduction subgroup at a suitably chosen split prime.

Finite graph truth tables stabilize along the same ultrafilter at each finite budget and agree by finite intersection. This produces compatible limit tables, not a single finite-stage valuation formula at all weights. The common alphabet requires separate surjections to each projection.

The stationary address construction uses nonzero linear activations of complete common packets and keeps total projected labels zero. Forest contraction and Cauchy–Binet yield the grounded Laplacian differential operator, including singular matrices. Anchor columns and balancing columns preserve the actual diagonal and label requirements.

Singular and varying path gadgets isolate the requested top-degree differential operator at the chosen address. The simultaneous argument takes the ordinary polynomial product before any Boolean reduction, then uses total differential degree to kill wrong or higher terms. Finite parameter choice and actual new-incidence realization remain separate.

For each fixed address dimension the proof first fixes every graph and output-weight budget, then selects a common finite stage and finally prime representatives by CRT and Dirichlet. It does not require an infinite intersection of stage conditions or surjectivity onto a product of projected alphabets.

The final contradiction uses the same Heegner coordinate, integral group-ring primitive, native genus bound and even-unit upper bound. Unit changes must belong to the integral group ring. Precision is fixed from the coefficient bound before address dimension and finite tests; the comparison uses the denominator coefficient bound, not an arbitrary numerator or inverse group-ring bound.

The next appendix announces a direct Gaussian ray-class construction of simultaneous primes and coprime adjacent norms, using Mitsui, nilsequence equidistribution/factorization and ordinary transference as substantive external inputs.
